paper_title: TRIC: A Thermal Resistance and Impedance Calculator for Electronic Packages

scenario.figure_or_table: Section 4.4, Figure 13 and Table 1 (multi-source eQFN, four layouts)
scenario.description: Static multi-source analysis of a 9 x 9 mm2 eQFN package with a 5 x 5 mm2 epad and a 4 x 4 mm2 die. The die has four 1 x 1 mm2 active areas (heat sources), each dissipating 0.5 W, in four layouts (#1 to #4). Layout positions appear only in the Figure 13 sketch. Table 1 reports temperature rises over ambient (K) at the four heat-source centers, the die center, and the die maximum.
scenario.architecture: Exposed-pad quad flat no-leads (eQFN) package, 9 x 9 mm2 body (0.9 mm thick per Section 2), 5 x 5 mm2 epad, 4 x 4 mm2 die with four 1 x 1 mm2 heat sources. Simulated with a purely conductive parametric detailed thermal model.
scenario.workload: Four 1 x 1 mm2 heat sources, each dissipating a constant 0.5 W (2 W total).
scenario.operating_point: Static (steady-state) temperature rise over ambient. The ambient and boundary conditions for this case are not stated explicitly in Section 4.4.

original_setup.solver: TRIC: a projection-based model-order-reduction solver. It reduces a purely conductive parametric detailed thermal model (Cartesian finite-volume mesh, multigrid iterative solves) to a compact thermal model. Section 4.4 reports static temperature rises for the multi-source eQFN case (PDF page 12).
original_setup.optimizer: None. The four heat-source layouts are compared by hand; no optimizer is used.
original_setup.controller: None. The case is static with constant power per source, so there is no controller or time-varying power profile.
original_setup.benchmark: Section 4.4 and Table 1 (PDF page 12): a 9 x 9 mm2 eQFN with a 5 x 5 mm2 epad and a 4 x 4 mm2 die. The die has four 1 x 1 mm2 heat sources of 0.5 W each, in four layouts. The paper says the maxima agree with FloTHERM to within 3%, but the FloTHERM maps are not shown. Section 4.3 (PDF page 10) separately reports a general TRIC vs FloTHERM comparison.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum over the whole die for Layout #1 (Table 1, column dTmax). Layout #1 is chosen because its row is cleanly legible in the packet text; the layout #2 row is garbled in the extracted text. The exact heat-source positions appear only in the Figure 13 sketch.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Spatial maximum over the die of the static (steady-state) temperature rise over ambient. It is a single value per layout, with no time averaging.

physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a 3D detailed thermal model of a molded eQFN package (die, die attach, epad, pins, mold, board). A 2D chip-level Studio placement cannot reproduce the vertical heat paths through the die attach, epad and board.

The paper uses JEDEC-style boundary conditions for the junction-to-ambient environment, with a board modelled as one parallelepiped of adjusted conductivity and pins as a homogenised block. Section 4.4 does not state the ambient or cooling boundary conditions for this case, so Studio cooling cannot be matched.

The solver differs. The paper uses a parametric projection-based compact model validated against FloTHERM finite-volume results, while Studio uses its own solver, so numerical results are not directly comparable.
The eQFN package has no interposer or 3D stacking, so those mismatches are not applicable, but the package-level geometry is not equivalent to a chiplet or interposer layout.

The paper has no optimizer, controller, reliability analysis or transient behaviour in this scenario (static case). Studio's optimizer or controller features therefore have no counterpart in the original setup.

studio_assumptions: No complete paper-derived floorplan can be built because the heat-source positions are available only in a figure sketch. Any Studio run would use a separate, illustrative 2D placement whose coordinates are generated by the runner and are not paper facts.

If an illustrative case is built, the published dimensions are the 4 x 4 mm2 die and four 1 x 1 mm2 sources, with 0.5 W each (2 W total, stated explicitly in the paper). No power is split by an unpublished rule.

Studio's bundled package and material assumptions would replace the paper's STMicroelectronics eQFN materials, pin and board homogenisation, and JEDEC boundary conditions. Temperatures from such a run must not be compared numerically with Table 1.
missing_inputs: Exact x/y coordinates of the four 1 x 1 mm2 heat sources for each layout (only in the Figure 13 sketch).
Die position and thickness, die attach, epad thickness, pin and board geometry, and material conductivities for the eQFN case.
Ambient temperature, heat transfer coefficients and board boundary conditions for the Section 4.4 simulation.
The FloTHERM temperature maps for the multi-source case (stated as not shown).
No paper-linked repositories, code, config files or supplementary data were found; the linked assets list is empty and no pinned assets were supplied.
Numeric values for layout #2 of Table 1 are garbled in the extracted text, so the layout #2 row is unreliable.
